heroHeadline: Chinese AI Labs Post Back-to-Back Open-Source Releases: Zhipu's GLM-5.3-Flash Runs on 100K Domestic Chips, Tencent Open-Sources 770B-Parameter Hy4
heroSubtitle: August 28, 2026 — China's domestic AI stack kept clearing milestones through the final week of August, again without a single event rising to crisis level. On August 24, Xiaomi unveiled the Xring D100, which it says is China's first high-computing-power smart-driving chip built on a 3nm process, manufactured by TSMC and capable of running 200-billion-parameter models locally, backed by more than 21 billion yuan ($3.1B) in chip R&D since the program restarted. On August 26, Chinese semiconductor ETFs plunged as investors reassessed valuations following CXMT's blockbuster Shanghai listing surge. The most significant developments came at week's end: on August 27, Zhipu AI (Z.ai) revealed that its new GLM-5.3-Flash model — previewed for a week under the code name 'Ox Alpha' — runs its entire global inference workload on a cluster of 100,000 domestically produced chips, widely believed to be Huawei Ascend hardware; the model set an OpenRouter platform record with 11 trillion tokens processed in its first three days, and Zhipu's Hong Kong-listed shares closed up more than 12%. The next day, August 28, Tencent open-sourced Hy4 preview, a 770-billion-parameter mixture-of-experts model with a context window exceeding 1 million tokens — the first Hunyuan model to help optimize its own training pipeline, which Tencent said lifted internal training/inference throughput by 31.8%. Separately, Bernstein's latest 2026 forecast — a sharp upward revision from its December 2025 outlook — now projects domestic chips will capture roughly 90% of China's high-end AI chip market this year, leaving Nvidia, AMD, and other foreign suppliers with about 10%. Taken together, the week reinforces a now-familiar pattern: major Chinese AI labs demonstrating large-scale inference and training entirely on home-grown silicon, with analyst market-share projections for domestic chips accelerating well beyond earlier estimates.
